environment: Python 3.14.7, Node test runner, scratch git repo from cli-runner; no network

cases.title: Hostile branch tails are refused or classified without crashes in scope
cases.given: Branch format sdlc/{name} and two other formats; slice commit 3ce4bff
cases.when: The attack corpus, newline tails, unicode digits and flag-like values go to parse and to the CLI
cases.then: No tail gains a kind the spec rows forbid; the CLI writes nothing
cases.expected: Spec rows 1 to 4 hold as written; no state change
cases.actual: Rows behave as the spec regexes say. Only a 4301-digit tail raises; no requirement covers it.

evidence.title: no tree change after 12 CLI attacks
evidence.inline: treeUnchanged true for every call (cli-runner tree diff)

attacks.charter: Explore parse with the trailing-newline family to find a hostile tail that gains a kind a clean tail would not get (spec §2 rows 1 to 4 anchors)
attacks.expected: null, or the same kind as the clean tail only if the spec regex allows it
attacks.observed: kind run n 3, milestone M-2, e2e M-2. Python $ matches before a final newline; tail keeps the newline. sdlc/M-2-e2e\n\n gives null. The regex text is the spec's own, so the guarantee is met as written. A git branch cannot hold a newline (check-ref-format).

attacks.charter: Explore parse with unicode digits to find a run or milestone id that differs from the ASCII form
attacks.expected: no spec statement; the plan says no test pins them
attacks.observed: Python \d matches them: run n 3; milestone id M-２ keeps its spelling. Seed.

attacks.charter: Explore parse with control characters and NUL to find a crash or a kind
Explore parse with the whole attack corpus (12 families) in 6 tail shapes under 3 formats to find a raise
attacks.input: 2814 calls: run-, M-, M-2-e2e-, run-3, M-2, M-2e2e plus each corpus value
attacks.observed: 21 calls raise ValueError: Exceeds the limit (4300 digits) for integer string conversion, for run-<more than 4300 digits>. All other 2793 return or null.

attacks.charter: Explore the CLI with the huge-integer tail to find a crash that breaks the one-JSON-object output
attacks.observed: Python traceback ValueError on stderr, no JSON, exit 1. git check-ref-format accepts the name; a ref this long cannot be a loose ref file on common file systems.

attacks.charter: Explore the CLI with flag-like and shell values to find option injection, command execution or a tree change
attacks.expected: exit 0 or 2 with JSON, tree unchanged
attacks.observed: --help and -x as separate argv give exit 2 JSON 'expected one argument'; the --branch= form parses them. The rest gives kind null. No file written, no ref change (treeUnchanged true).

attacks.charter: Explore row 4 with a slash inside the area to find a kind the spec forbids
attacks.observed: kind e2e-area, id M-2, area a/b. Noted, not failed, per the ADR.

attacks.charter: Explore the CLI with newline tails to confirm that the CLI and the function agree
attacks.observed: CLI gives kind run n 3, the same as the function.

seeds.title: parse raises ValueError for run-N or attempt-N with more than 4300 digits
seeds.detail: int(value) in parse hits Python's int string limit. The CLI prints a traceback and no JSON, against spec section 2 'every command prints one JSON object'. next-action.py would crash if such a branch head existed. Guard the conversion or cap the digits. No requirement in R-102 to R-105 states it.

seeds.title: Trailing newline accepted by $ in rows 1 to 4
seeds.detail: parse('sdlc/{name}','sdlc/run-3\n') gives kind run. Use re.fullmatch or \Z to match the strict intent. Real branches cannot hold a newline, so impact is low. The spec gives the regex with $.

seeds.title: Unicode digits accepted in run-N and M-N
seeds.detail: Python \d matches Arabic-Indic and fullwidth digits, so run-٣ is n 3 and M-２ is a milestone with a non-ASCII id. Use [0-9] or re.ASCII.

seeds.title: Slash in an e2e-area tail is classified as e2e-area
seeds.detail: M-2-e2e-a/b gives area a/b. The ADR keeps this behavior.
